title: Machito band instrumentation and adding the conga
summary: He explains starting with two trumpets and saxes, then three trumpets, extra sax and conga.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: That was -- and I know that that was about the time the Palladium got going. Now, I'd like to jump back a little to the early great days, you know, the mid-'40s of
the Machito band and have you talk a little about the musicians and what you were playing. You were the first -- were you not the first New York band to use a congo rhythm? regularly
Can you get into the music and the sound a bit?

Well, I tell you what the sound -- the band started -- I start the band with two trumpets. I can put a whole lot of musicians, but I was afraid nobody was going to pay. The average band in those days was one trumpet and maybe one violin and marimba, all kind of stuff like that, you know. RUMBA

So I got it with three SAXES (inaudible) and two trumpets. But for me playing saxophone, trumpet too. So when I play BALLAD (inaudible), I had the BALLAD (inaudible) arranged to four saxophones and one trumpet. And when I get (inaudible) change it to two trumpets and three saxes. So I (inaudible) before I went on to another one.
(Inaudible) number I play trumpet alone, and that's -- we started like that. Then I went to three trumpets. (Inaudible). Then I went to another saxophone. Then I put a conga.
I put the conga in 19 -- I put the conga in
(inaudible) Conga nightclub in 1942, about '42, yeah, '42 or '43.
